paragraphs.text: Those who disbelieve and turn people away from Allah's path will have their deeds wasted. Those who believe, do righteous deeds, and accept what was sent down upon Muhammad will have their misdeeds removed and their condition improved. The passage contrasts falsehood with truth. It describes fighting, securing captives, and then releasing them by favor or ransom when the war has ended. Those killed in Allah's cause will not lose their deeds. Allah guides them, improves their condition, and admits them to Paradise. Believers are urged to support Allah, and He will support them and make their feet firm. By contrast, those who reject what Allah revealed lose their deeds. The passage points to the end of earlier peoples as a warning, and says that Allah protects believers while disbelievers have no protector. The passage explains that this testing lets some people be tested through others. Those killed in Allah's cause receive guidance and a better condition, and Paradise has been made known to them. The contrast is repeated: disbelievers face misery, while Allah is the protector of those who believe. The earlier cities show that strength alone did not save them.

Believers who do righteous deeds will enter gardens with rivers, while disbelievers enjoy life as grazing livestock do and face the Fire. Many cities stronger than Makkah were destroyed, with no helper for them. The passage asks whether someone guided by clear evidence is like someone who follows desires after evil work has seemed attractive. Paradise is described with rivers of water, milk, wine, and purified honey, fruit, and forgiveness from the Lord. This is compared with the Fire and scalding water. Some people listen to the Messenger, then ask others what he said; they follow their desires and have sealed hearts. Those who accept guidance receive more guidance and righteousness. The description also mentions that Allah increases the guided in guidance and gives them righteousness. It contrasts those on clear evidence with those led by desires, and asks whether their outcomes can be alike.
